newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures end quiet day down slightly.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures end quiet day down slightly.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures cut their gains in afternoon trade to end slightly lower after a very quiet session.
After firm morning trade, the market's focus switched to worries about corporate supply this week and talk of a hedge fund seller of September Treasury bond futures, traders said.
September slipped through Monday's 110-17/32 session low to post a new low for the week at 110-12/32.
"I still think we're in a kind of consolidation mode if nothing else," one 10-year note futures trader said. He said action was light on the late decline, as it had been all day.
"We eroded a little lower, but unfortunately there was not any news out," he said.

Late in the session, U.S. adjusted retail sales were reported up 2.3 percent in the first week of June versus May, according to Redbook Research. A few traders said the strong Redbook may have also weighed on prices.
A buoyant tone early stemmed from ideas the overall tone was still solid after Monday's losses on profit-taking.
Traders said the more than 17,000 contract decline Monday in Treasury bond futures open interest pointed to liquidation, not a change in trend.
September crawled to the upper 110-00 handle near midday, but failed to test resistance at 111-00 and cut its gains.
Some traders said that failure also helped spawn the afternoon downdraft.
The data line-up was light on Tuesday, and no economic news was expected Wednesday.

Early in the session, BTM/Schroders reported U.S. adjusted chain store sales up 0.7 percent. The Richmond Federal Reserve Bank May manufacturing shipments index rose to 21 from 15 in April. New orders fell to 16 from 25.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan speaks at 2000 CDT/0100 GMT Tuesday night.

At the close, September T-bonds were down 2/32 at 110-17/32, 10-yr notes fell 3/32 to 108-3/32, munis rose 2/32 to 118-7/32, Sept bills were down 0.005 point at 94.665, Dec Euros fell 0.010 to 93.810.
